title: Bundled SKU pricing approval flow with Security Questionnaire linkage
creator: Caroline Nguyen
description:
Context: Sales and Solutions Engineering increasingly request combined product bundles (Dedicated + Console retention add-ons + Optimize) with bespoke discounts tied to completed Security Questionnaires (SQ). Current pricebook and approval ladder do not reflect SQ-linked conditional discounts or multi-SKU bundling. This creates inconsistent approvals, manual back-and-forth with Legal/RevOps, and delayed deal cycles.

Objective: Define a clear internal approval flow and pricebook update process that: 1) supports bundled SKU offers with templated discount tiers, 2) ties discount eligibility to an SQ score and contract/capacity terms, and 3) enables delegated approvals up to defined thresholds to reduce friction for common mid-market deals.

Proposed solution (high level):
- Add a new 'Bundled Enterprise SKU' section to the pricebook with three suggested discount tiers (Tier A: standard bundle 0-10% off list, Tier B: SQ-qualified 11-25%, Tier C: strategic 26-40% with exec signoff).
- Implement an SQ linkage: RevOps will flag deals with an SQ score >= 85 as eligible for Tier B. Tier C requires Legal and Sales VP approval and justification in the deal comment.
- Approval ladder:
  - Sales rep -> AE manager (auto-approve up to 15% for Tier A/B)
  - AE manager -> RevOps delegated approver (16-25%)
  - >25% -> Sales VP + Legal signoff + Pricing review (manual)
- Automate gating in CRM: add 'SQ-eligible' checkbox + attach SQ report link. Where possible, pre-populate recommended tier in deal desk UI.
- Create lightweight pricebook amendment doc and rollout notes for sales and partner teams.

Acceptance criteria:
- Updated pricebook entry published in Confluence and synced to the internal ratecard within 2 weeks of ticket close.
- CRM automation (recommended tier pre-fill + SQ flag) prototyped in a sandbox and documented in the engineering handoff.
- Delegated approval workflow configured in Deal Desk with clear SLA (24h for delegated tiers).
- One pilot deal completed end-to-end (Sales -> RevOps -> Billing) using the new flow and retrospective notes captured.

Trade-offs & open questions:
- Trade-off: stricter SQ thresholds reduce risk but may increase time-to-close for strategic customers. Consider a grace process where Solutions Eng can request timed exception.
- Trade-off: aggressive delegation speeds up mid-market deals but slightly reduces centralized billing oversight; mitigate with automated weekly telemetry of delegated approvals.
- Open question: Should usage-based discounts be calculated as a blended % across SKUs or as per-SKU caps? Need RevOps/Finance input (see dependencies).

Implementation plan / milestones:
1) 2025-03-03 to 2025-03-10: Draft pricebook text + SQ-threshold proposal (PM lead).
2) 2025-03-11 to 2025-03-14: Legal & Finance review; finalize delegated thresholds.
3) 2025-03-15 to 2025-03-22: Engineering prototype CRM gating + Deal Desk delegation config (sfdc prototype), RevOps automations.
4) 2025-03-23 to 2025-03-28: Pilot with two AE teams; capture telemetry and iterate.

Deliverables: updated Confluence pricebook page, sample Deal Desk approval checklist, CRM prototype PR, rollout email + training deck for AEs, pilot retrospective notes.

Notes on security/compliance: SQ linkage requires attaching a sanitized SQ PDF to the deal record. Ensure PII is not stored in the CRM attachment field; use a secure RevOps S3 bucket link. Legal requested a checklist to ensure only redacted SQs are used in approval decisions.
